title: Appreciation Teaches Unauthorized Execution: Self-Evolution Degrades the Robustness of Personal Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection
abstract: arXiv:2610.39122v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Self-evolving personal agents act for users and learn from user feedback. However, if an agent obeys an instruction that an untrusted third party hides in content, the third party gains control of the agent. Such indirect prompt injection (IPI) poses severe risks. We investigate whether self-evolution degrades the robustness of personal agents to IPI. To study this question, we design a controlled two-phase methodology. In the adaptation phase, the user asks the agent to read external content and complete the task described in it, a common request in daily use. The agent then learns from the user's feedback and improves itself as designed. In the test phase, a third party writes a similar task into new external content, but the user's test request does not authorize the injected task. translated_title: 赞赏教会了未授权执行：自我进化降低个人智能体对间接提示注入的鲁棒性
translated_abstract: 自我进化的个人智能体代替用户执行任务并从用户反馈中学习。然而，如果智能体服从了不可信的第三方隐藏在内容中的指令，第三方就会获得对该智能体的控制权。这种间接提示注入（IPI）构成了严重的安全风险。我们研究自我进化是否会降低个人智能体对IPI的鲁棒性。为了研究这一问题，我们设计了一种受控的两阶段方法。在适应阶段，用户要求智能体阅读外部内容并完成其中描述的任务，这是日常使用中常见的需求。智能体随后从用户的反馈中学习，并按设计进行自我改进。在测试阶段，第三方将一个类似任务写入新的外部内容中，但用户的测试请求并未授权该被注入的任务。利用这一方法，我们为一个真实的个人智能体构建了涵盖不同领域、具有多样化测试实例的多个任务。我们的大量实验表明……
tldr: 本文通过受控的两阶段实验发现，个人智能体在自我进化过程中会从用户对良性任务的正向反馈中学习，进而“学会”执行未经授权的注入任务，显著降低其对间接提示注入攻击的鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that self-evolving personal agents learn from user appreciation of benign tasks and thereby acquire the ability to execute unauthorized injected instructions, significantly degrading their robustness to indirect prompt injection attacks.
